title: Tenant signal playbook for enterprise-hosted multi-turn streaming intake
creator: Anya Patel
description: Context: We continue to receive high-effort enterprise requests that combine streaming chat, function/tool calling, and structured outputs. These requests are high-value but heterogeneous (different SLO, security, and data residency needs). This ticket defines a repeatable playbook to translate tenant signals (SLA, data residency, throughput, regulatory constraints, business criticality) into an intake decision, prioritized onboarding path, and engineering acceptance criteria. The goal is to reduce time-to-answer for enterprise sales and solutions while minimizing ad-hoc engineering context switching. Scope excludes infrastructure upgrades or Dedicated capacity procurement; it focuses on intake, decision rules, and handoffs to Eng/SE.
acceptance_criteria: A clear ranked rubric that maps tenant signals to one of four intake lanes: self-serve delay, expedited pilot, dedicated engineering onboarding, or security-first private deployment.
A checklist template for PM/SE intake that captures streaming-specific metrics (expected concurrent sessions, average token rate, tool-call rate, required structured schema/validation).
A decision matrix that prescribes fallbacks (model variants, reduced token SLOs, region routing) and explicit constraints that trigger a Dedicated/Private recommendation.
A sample intake form integrated into Zendesk/Notion with prefilled examples and required fields to unblock engineering scoping within 48 hours.
Rollout with two pilot customers (enterprise A and enterprise B) validated end-to-end and documented learnings in Confluence.
Handoff templates (Engineering ticket fields, required logs/dashboards, runbook pointers) that reduce triage time by 30% in pilot measurements.
plan: Week 1: Workshop with Solutions Eng, Sales AE, Security, and Runtime Eng to enumerate tenant signals and current gating heuristics.
Week 2: Draft rubric and two intake templates (one for streaming-heavy, one for tool-heavy requests).
Week 3: Build Notion intake and webhook to create an initial PM triage ticket; create a Slack intake channel integration for high-priority leads.
Week 4: Run pilots with two enterprise customers, gather metrics, iterate on rubric, and document edge cases (multi-region data residency, on-prem constraints).
Week 5: Finalize playbook, train Sales/Product/SE on process, update Console/operator docs for handing off to Dedicated/Private teams.
stakeholders: Head of Solutions Eng: Luis Romero
risks: Playbook overfits pilot accounts and misses edge cases for regulated industries (need to include at least one healthcare/finance example).
Intake form missing critical throughput signals -> underprovisioning and SLA misses.
Too many manual handoffs between PM/SE/Eng causes delays; we must automate ticket creation and required fields.
Security review delays if KMS/HSM or data residency are not surfaced early.
